svg.title: Precursors
svg.desc: What coding harnesses already have (the decision ledger, a thin effect ledger, git underneath) and what they're missing (the obligation ledger, the effect taxonomy, action gates, shared-state coordination) — which is what the treatise calls the ceiling.
svg.text: Precursors
What the harnesses already have, what they're missing — and why the missing part has a name.
HAVE
✓ the decision ledger — the transcript
append-only · ordered · used as memory, not replayed verbatim (the right move)
◐ a thin effect ledger — the snapshot
coarse (whole-file / whole-tree) · local files only · where it exists at all
✓ git underneath — a real journal to lean on
commits · branches · stash · reflog · restore · revert · worktrees
MISSING
✗ the obligation ledger
"this push needs reverting if the build fails"
✗ the effect taxonomy
reversible / partial / irreversible — and acting on it
✗ action gates on push / publish / deploy
approval before the irreversible
✗ coordination through *shared* journaled state
worktrees + leases + merge-base awareness,
What's missing = what the treatise calls THE CEILING.
What's present = mostly THE FLOOR (git) plus a decent transcript.
The working-tree / worktree / merge interplay
is where the floor holds — and where it runs out.
Coding harnesses are proto-journals, and the prototype is honest about what it is:
small · local · optimistic · single-actor.
Scale the world — a second agent, a remote, CI, a publish, a deploy — and the prototype breaks in exactly the ways
Sections V and XIV predict. The fix isn't more rewind. It's the ceiling: effect classification, action gates, compensation
handles, and coordination through shared journaled state — instead of N private rewind stacks racing on one checkout.
